note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with progressive lower back pain of three weeks duration without radicular symptoms. No recent trauma reported. Physical exam reveals paraspinal tenderness without neurological deficits.  
- Differential diagnosis includes lumbar strain (high likelihood), degenerative disc disease (moderate likelihood), and less likely infection or malignancy. Management includes conservative treatment and follow-up.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Lower Back Pain
- Three-week history of progressively worsening lower back pain localized to the lumbar region, no radiation or neurologic symptoms.
- Pertinent negatives: no numbness, weakness, bowel/bladder changes reported.
- Physical exam: paraspinal muscle tenderness, no neurological deficits.
- Differential diagnosis: 
  - Lumbar strain (High) — most consistent with history and exam.
  - Degenerative disc disease (Moderate) — possible given age and symptoms.
  - Spinal infection/malignancy (Low) — no systemic signs or red flags noted.

Medications:
- Acetaminophen dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Past Medical History:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Not documented.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Paraspinal tenderness in lumbar region.
- No neurological deficits detected.

Plan:
- Advise conservative management with rest, acetaminophen, and avoidance of heavy lifting.
- Recommend follow-up in two weeks to reassess symptoms.
- Consider imaging if symptoms worsen or neurologic signs develop.

Quality checks:

- Medication dosing details not documented.
